claims.text: The baseline APS process uses FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution.
APS deposition using the 15–45 μm feedstock produces insufficient coating thickness.
Changing the feedstock distribution to approximately 45–70 μm and optimizing APS parameters will increase coating thickness relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The larger feedstock and optimized APS parameters will produce a more continuous and dense coating.
The intervention will preserve microstructural integrity and low as-sprayed oxidation.
A larger particle of the same material contains greater volume and mass than a smaller particle.
Recalibrating plasma power, spray distance, and related APS parameters can ensure complete melting of the 45–70 μm particles.
Fully molten APS particles form well-flattened splats.
The greater molten mass of the larger particles will produce thicker splats.
Thicker, well-flattened splats will coalesce more effectively into a continuous, dense deposit.
Larger splats will exhibit enhanced inter-splat bonding.
Deposition of more material in each particle-impact event will build a thicker coating.
Fine-tuning APS parameters will prevent deposition defects and minimize oxidation.
Using an inert or otherwise controlled spraying atmosphere will help avoid excessive oxidation during APS deposition.
The resulting thicker coating will be suitable for service as a thermal-barrier-system bond coat.
The intervention remains effective only if the larger particles are completely melted and deposited uniformly.
Inadequate particle heating can leave partially molten particles in an APS coating.
Improper APS parameter settings could produce microstructural heterogeneity.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes recalibration of APS parameters, while the experiment says all other spray parameters are held constant after a 'necessary recalibration.' It is therefore unclear whether the two feedstocks are tested under identical parameters or different optimized parameters, which confounds attribution of any thickness change to particle size alone.
The proposal is framed as a single intervention but combines two independently outcome-relevant changes: a larger particle-size distribution and optimization of multiple APS parameters.
